claims.text: DFT simulations combined with machine-learning algorithms can predict and optimize alloy compositions.
Alloy compositions optimized using DFT and machine learning can improve oxidation resistance in metallic materials.
Computationally optimized alloy compositions can improve high-temperature performance.
The proposed method applies under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
An optimized alloy composition is the structural mediator between computational optimization and improved oxidation resistance.
Computational modeling of material properties and machine-learning-based optimization constitute the proposed mechanism.
Computational power limits can constrain the proposed method.
Machine-learning model accuracy can constrain the proposed method.
DFT and machine-learning predictions may not accurately transfer to real-world high-temperature oxidation behavior.
Oxidation rate, scale formation, and material degradation can be used to compare computationally optimized alloys with standard alloys.
Failure of optimized alloys to show significantly improved oxidation resistance over standard alloys would falsify the hypothesis.
